label: All three playbook scenarios are single-question and fixture-fed: the hook scenario pipes one redacted toolu_fixture payload, the sweep scenario replays two fixture transcripts, and the writer scenario posts one operatorDecisions entry. Every claim they can carry is a single-shot claim.

No scenario asserts the consumption loop closes, and the save-writer scenario would pass with recordConsumedKeys broken: its last step is an existence test on consumed.jsonl, it never reads the row count or calls pendingRecords, so a build that wrote the row and appendix but never consumed the key satisfies every expected signal including BYTE_IDENTICAL.

No playbook scenario mentions the Stop-hook nudge or the word pending, although 001 claims a Stop-hook line tells the operator answers are still waiting for a save; the only operator-facing signal that consumption failed has zero scenario coverage.

The hook scenario proves registration, mirroring and the kill switch but not 001 REQ-009's UNKNOWN-and-disabled discipline: no scenario checks a probe file status, a README cell or a disabled adapter, so AC-009's four-runtime claim rests on 003's planned refusal test, not on playbook evidence.

sweep-transcript.mjs is never invoked from the command line by any scenario: the sweep scenario's only CLI run is sweep-devin twice, so chat-question detection - the surface 005 must preserve and extend - is proven by a node --test suite and by nothing else.

The OpenCode reader is exercised only through its test suite, and 001's one live opencode.db run recovered 0 records in 3 ms, so the newest session_message layout stays inferred and the scenario cannot close the gap that 004 exists to close.

The adapter process.cwd fallback that iteration 1 flagged as able to write outside the project is never exercised: both hook commands set CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so the branch is unreachable in the evidence even though the scenario triage names its symptom.

The nothing-written-to-the-real-repository check is blind to the state directory it protects: the save-writer scenario uses git status --short --untracked-files=no, which hides untracked files over a gitignored state dir, and 006 REQ-002 has the same shape with --short and no --ignored. Two packets, one shared blind check.

Dedupe is proven only for the Devin sweep via recovered 2 then recovered 0; neither the hook path nor the transcript path is re-run, and all three scenarios grade PASS or FAIL only, so the working scenarios set a two-mark precedent that 006's four-mark gate departs from.

The numbering is a build order while the dependency runs the other way: every child 002 to 005 carries a final requirement whose evidence lands in 006's results matrix and a final task to produce it, so reading 6 of 6 as build-006-last makes the series unclosable. 006's scenario authoring needs only 065's format, so it can precede the sibling builds.

006 REQ-011 declares that siblings add stages without renumbering, but all four siblings commit only to a results-matrix row and not one adds a stage: one inheritance mechanism with no counterparty, which is why the 13-row gate in AC-005 is unstable. Pick one mechanism and say which.

Iteration 2's inference that 002 to 005 each inherit the four-mark verdict vocabulary is refuted by one grep: DEVIATION, N/A and SKIP appear in exactly one child acceptance file, 006 AC-005, with 006 REQ-003. The mapping 065 assigned to 043 is a two-line fix in one packet, not a series-wide edit.

002's --apply mapping lives in gitignored consumed.jsonl and is therefore per-machine, but the matcher is deterministic and sha256-guarded on its input, so a re-clone can rebuild the identical mapping in one command. State rebuild-by-re-derivation as a tested property instead of planning new committed state.

002 AC-006 is the series' only criterion that a session ends with nothing pending and the Stop hook silent, but it is a one-shot repair of one real session whose precondition - records 29 and 30 consumed by an external series-parent save - sits outside the packet. Keep it and restate the property as a repeatable check in 006.

The carried-forward nuance is still unowned: 002 REQ-002 and AC-003 refuse when two rows tie for one record, but nothing addresses two records whose different answers match the same row. REQ-002's answer-equality rule probably refuses the second by construction, and the packet must say so, because a table row holds one answer.

Refusal reporting has one shape in 003 - an n/a README cell with an observed reason pinned by a test - a weaker and different shape in 004, and no criterion at all in 002, which prints a per-record reason but never counts refusals, so pending equals zero survives as the implied handoff metric despite 002's own shortened-option and line-break measurements.

Orphan session queues and the missing release path are owned by nobody: no child enumerates the queue directory or offers an un-consume path, and 004 REQ-006's cross-runtime nudge makes both worse by adding sessions and queue files with no enumeration. 002 already owns consumed.jsonl semantics, so the orphan scan and a --release belong there rather than in a seventh child.

004 carries a precondition it cannot satisfy alone: its redacted real session_message fixture must be the artifact of its own live probe, described as two steps in an order that does not say so, and 001's live store yielded zero question calls. State the fixture-provenance rule and give REQ-003 the same honest-escape clause REQ-005 already has.

005's own risk row names its real failure mode - 3 of the 4 baseline candidates answer no earlier question because the reply moved on - yet no acceptance criterion and no 006 stage asserts that a non-answering reply writes no decision row; the mitigation is prose in a save-step instruction.

Nine assertions the 006 conversation scenario must carry that the playbook set does not: pending reaches zero with one consumed row per answer; the per-turn nudge sequence and session.nudge counts; the process question stays out of queue and anchors; the adapter with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset; a --ignored repository-state check; a chat candidate through the sweep CLI plus no row for a non-answering reply; a second differing answer not consumed under the first answer's Q id; counted refusals; and the save path or matcher being the consumer. 006 already carries two of the nine.

A scenario can only certify the properties its assertion set can fail on: an existence check on consumed.jsonl cannot certify consumption, and git status --untracked-files=no over a gitignored state directory cannot certify that nothing was written there.

A cross-packet inheritance clause is only real when the consuming packets implement it: 006 REQ-011 requires siblings to add stages and no sibling does, so the clause constrains nobody and the row-count gate stays ambiguous.

direction: Treating 006 results-matrix rows and 006 stages as interchangeable carriers of sibling evidence
reason: No sibling adds a stage and AC-005 fixes the Claude file at 13 rows, so the two mechanisms are mutually exclusive in practice.

direction: Splitting 004's cross-runtime nudge into a new child
reason: It is the same Stop hook 001 shipped, widened by runtime, and its evidence is still a nudge count in 006's matrix, so a seventh packet would have no independent artifact.

direction: Assuming the four-mark verdict vocabulary spreads across 002 to 005
reason: One grep over the five child acceptance files returns only 006 AC-005, refuting the iteration-2 inference that each sibling needs the same edit.
